# Time series, cointegration and macroeconomic forecasting

Course materials, hands-on R labs and applied Pakistani case studies from
**Prof. Dr. Zahid Asghar**, School of Economics, Quaid-i-Azam University.

Everything here is reproducible: each lecture and lab is a Quarto document that
pulls real data — SBP, PBS, World Bank, Yahoo Finance, UN Comtrade — and runs the
estimation in front of you.

14 lecture decks · 10 hands-on labs · 90+ datasets · all code in R

## What the course covers

The sequence is deliberate. We begin with the single question that decides
everything else — *is this series stationary?* — because getting it wrong produces
regressions that look magnificent and mean nothing. From there the course builds
outward: modelling a single series, quantifying how wrong the forecast is likely
to be, then moving to systems of series where the interesting economics lives.

| Block | Topics | Lectures |
|---|---|---|
| **Foundations** | Stationarity, unit root testing, spurious regression | 1–5 |
| **Univariate modelling** | ARIMA, forecast uncertainty and evaluation, ARCH/GARCH volatility | 6–8 |
| **Multivariate systems** | Cointegration and VECM, ARDL bounds testing, VAR, structural VAR | 9–13 |
| **Panel data** | Fixed and random effects, panel unit roots | 14 |

## Software

All work is done in **R** with Quarto. The core stack is the tidyverse plus
`fable`/`feasts` for forecasting, `urca` and `tseries` for unit root and
cointegration testing, `vars` and `svars` for VAR work, `ARDL` for bounds
testing, and `plm` for panels. Selected Python equivalents live in `R/methods/`
for students who prefer them.

``` r
install.packages(c("tidyverse", "fpp3", "fable", "feasts", "tsibble",
                   "urca", "tseries", "vars", "svars", "ARDL", "plm",
                   "readxl", "quantmod", "WDI"))
```

## How this repository is organised

| Folder | What lives there |
|---|---|
| `lectures/` | The 14 lecture documents that make up the site |
| `labs/` | Hands-on R walkthroughs, including `labs/r-foundations/` for students new to R |
| `applications/` | Applied Pakistan studies — remittances, exchange rate, exports, tax, solar prices, KSE |
| `assessments/` | Exams, assignment briefs and the term paper specification |
| `slides/` | Standalone decks (PPTX and revealjs) |
| `R/` | Standalone scripts: `setup/`, `textbook/` (Enders, Stock–Watson), `methods/`, `applications/` |
| `data/` | Datasets used across the course; `data/large/` holds files too big for git |
| `references/` | Reading material, IMF forecasting module, xts/zoo chapters |
| `shiny/` | Small interactive apps |
| `docs/` | **Generated site output — never edit by hand** |

## Rebuilding the site

``` bash
quarto render          # writes the full site into docs/
```

GitHub Pages serves `docs/` on the `main` branch. Rendered chunk output is
frozen under `_freeze/`, so a rebuild only re-executes documents you have
actually changed.
